newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana likely to announce investor package.
newsitem.headline: Botswana likely to announce investor package.

text.p: A package on liberalising Botswana's exchange controls to attract foreign investors will probably be announced soon, a Bank of Botswana official said on Tuesday.

"The faster we go (towards liberalising exchange control) the more incentive there will be for investors. A package should be announced soon," Bank of Botswana research director Keith Jefferis told a business forum, a day after the country's budget was announced by Finance Minister Festus Mogae.
Business people from finance and industry sectors criticised the budget saying it was consumer-driven instead of aimed at drawing investors.
Botswana Stock Exchange chief executive Alan Norrie said there was nothing in the budget to encourage investment.
"A 9.5 percent (public service) salary award, marginal rate tax down from 30 percent to 25 per cent and a lower tax threshold, could push disposal incomes by 10.5 percent," Norrie said.
"In investor terms, it is neutral," he added.
He criticised Botswana's exchange rate policy of indirectly linking the Botswana pula to the South African rand to protect non-diamond exports, but said he hoped Botswana would free the pula.
"I would like to see an environment in which a prudent businessman would reinvest his profits in Botswana," Norrie said.
Baledzi Gaolathe, managing director of Debswana, a 50-50 partnership between the Botswanan government and diamond giant De Beers, cautioned business to expect a further depreciation of the pula.
"Do not look for surprises, There is no doubt that the pula will continue to circulate around the rand and that currency will further depreciate," Gaolathe said.
But Jefferis supported Botswana's exchange rate policy and said it would not be changed.
"There is nothing we can do if a neighbour's currency is unstable," he said. "We have to live with that," he added.

The pula -- which shadows South Africa's rand -- stood at 35 U.S. cents at the start of 1996 but had fallen to 27 cents by the end of the December. This year it has strengthened only slightly to 28 cents, despite the strong rally in the rand.
